title: FATHER, LET MY ACTIONS REFLECT YOUR GOODNESS
text: Good morning. Good morning. Good morning. I want you to take a deep breath and acknowledge that you are alive this morning. Not just alive biologically, alive spiritually, alive with purpose. Alive with the breath of God in your lungs. Every morning you open your eyes is not a coincidence. It is a commission. God did not wake you up this morning simply to exist. He woke you up because there is something he needs to express through you today. There is a dimension of his goodness that the world around you will only see if you show up and show up correctly. Lift your hands right where you are this morning. Lift them and say, "Father, I am here. I am available. Let this day be a reflection of who you are. I want to minister to you this morning from a place of urgency in my spirit. Because there is a generation that is waking up today and they're going into the world, into offices, into markets, into schools, into neighborhoods, into families carrying the name of God and some of them are about to misrepresent him again. Some of them are about to step into situations where the authentic goodness of God is needed and they're about to offer a counterfeit. And the Holy Spirit woke me up this morning with a burden. A holy burden. A burning that would not let me be quiet and the burden is this. The world needs to see God and the only way they will see God today is through the people who carry him. Let me take you to 1 Peter chapter 2 and verse 12. This is Peter writing to believers who are scattered, who are in the minority, who are surrounded by a culture that is hostile to their faith. And this is what he says. "Having your conduct honorable among the Gentiles, that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works which they observe glorify God in the day of visitation." This is a morning word. This is a word for how you carry yourself today. Peter says, "Live so honorably, behave so consistently, conduct yourself with such integrity and goodness that even the people who started out speaking evil about you, even the people who question your faith, even the people who doubted whether your Christianity was real, will end up glorifying God because of what they saw in your life. That is powerful. That is not just a moral instruction. That is a spiritual strategy. Peter is telling the early church your behavior is warfare. Your conduct is an evangelistic tool. Your consistent good works will do what your words sometimes cannot do. Because people can argue with your theology, they can debate your doctrine, they can dismiss your preaching, but they cannot argue with a transformed life. They cannot explain away someone who genuinely loves when they have every reason to hate. They cannot rationalize someone who gives with their whole heart in a season of scarcity. They cannot dismiss someone whose peace defies their circumstances. The life of a genuine believer is the most powerful apologetic on the earth. And so this morning the question is not whether you will go to church on Sunday. The question is not whether you have a devotional life. The question is not whether you can quote scriptures. The question this morning is simple and it is direct. When you walk out of that door today and step into your day, will the people you encounter have an encounter with God through you? That is the question. I want to establish something in your spirit this morning that is going to change the way you approach every single day. Micah 6 to 8 says, "He has shown you, oh man, what is good. And what the Lord require of you but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?" Three things, just three things. But these three things encompass the entire ethical and moral demand of the kingdom of God. Do justly, love mercy, walk humbly. Let me unpack this for you. To do justly means to be a person of fairness and righteousness in all your dealings, not just when the law is watching, not just when your pastor is in the room. Not just when there is a consequence attached to your behavior. But in the quiet places, in the hidden transactions, in the moments when no human being could ever find out, you choose what is right because the God you serve is righteous and his righteousness must find expression through you. Justice is not just a legal concept, it is a character attribute of God. Psalm 89:2-14 says, "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne." When you do justly in your daily interactions, you are building on the same foundation that God's throne is built on. To love mercy is deeper than just be merciful. The word love in this context indicates a posture of heart. You do not merely practice mercy when you feel like it. You love mercy. You are drawn to it. You lean toward it. When someone makes a mistake that affects you, your first instinct is not punishment. It is restoration. When someone falls short of what they owe you, your default is not retaliation. It is grace. This is because you remember what you were before mercy found you. Titus 3:2-3 says, "We ourselves were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another." But when the kindness and the love of God our savior toward man appeared, he saved us. When you remember where mercy found you, it becomes very difficult to withhold mercy from someone else. And to walk humbly with your God means that you carry the consciousness of his presence through every moment of every day. Not just in the prayer room, not just in the sanctuary, but in the traffic that is making you late, in the meeting that is testing your patience, in the conversation that is triggering your insecurity, in the moment when pride is telling you to assert yourself and crush someone who made you look small. In all of those moments, you are walking with God, you are conscious that he sees. You are aware that his spirit is within you and that consciousness governs your conduct. Let me speak to someone specifically this morning. There is someone listening right now who is heading into a difficult environment today. Maybe it is a workplace where corruption is the culture. Maybe it is a family situation where dysfunction is the norm. Maybe it is a social circle where compromise is expected and the temptation is to blend in. The pressure is to go along. The path of least resistance is to become like the environment rather than changing the environment and I want to speak to you directly this morning. You were not placed there to blend in. You were placed there to be a catalyst. You were placed there to be the salt that prevents decay and the light that overcomes darkness. Matthew 5:13 and 14, you are the salt of the earth, you are the light of the world. Salt does not ask for permission to do its work. When salt enters a corrupt environment, it automatically begins to corruption. When light enters a dark room, it does not negotiate with the darkness. It does not say, "Excuse me, darkness. Would you mind moving?" Light simply shines and darkness disappears because darkness is not a thing. It is the absence of a thing. Darkness is the absence of light. And when light enters, there is nothing for darkness to do but leave. You are the light in that environment. You do not need to make a speech. You do not need to campaign. You just need to be who God made you to be consistently, faithfully, daily and the environment will shift. Daniel chapter 6 is one of my favorite passages for this teaching. Daniel was in Babylon. He was a captive. He was in a foreign land surrounded by a foreign culture serving under a foreign king. Every social pressure told him to assimilate. Every political reality suggested that survival required compromise. But the Bible tells us in Daniel 6:2-3 that Daniel distinguished himself above all the governors and satraps because an excellent spirit was in him. His excellence was so undeniable that even his enemies could not find a charge against him. They searched for fault, they investigated his conduct, they went through his records. And the verdict in verse 4 says that they could find no charge or fault because he was faithful and there was no error or fault found in him. That is the testimony God wants to write over your life. Faithful, no fault, no inconsistency, not sinless perfection, but a genuine and consistent alignment between your profession and your practice. Between the God you confess in your prayers and the God people encounter in your actions. Now, I want to go somewhere this morning that I feel very strongly about. I want to talk about morning intentionality. There is a reason we are gathering in the morning. There is a reason the Holy Spirit leads us to seek God at the beginning of the day. Psalm 5:2-3 says, "My voice you shall hear in the morning, oh Lord. In the morning I will direct it to you and I will look up." David had a morning protocol, a morning orientation toward God. And that orientation was not just about getting information from God or getting blessings from God. It was about aligning his spirit, his soul, and his body with the will of God before he stepped into the demands of the day. Proverbs 4:23 says, "Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it spring the issues of life." The morning is your heart maintenance time. It is when you come before God and you say, "Lord, check my heart, search me and try me, remove every residue of last night's frustration, remove every seed of bitterness that was planted by yesterday's disappointment, remove every wrong attitude that crept in through the back door of my weariness. Cleanse my heart so that what flows out of me today is clean. What flows out of me today is from you. What flows out of me today is good because you are good. This is why the enemy fights your morning. This is why there is always something competing for your attention in the morning. Your phone wants you, the news wants you, your appetite wants you. Your to-do list wants you, your anxiety wants you. Everything is competing for the first fruits of your consciousness. And if the enemy can capture your morning, he has a head start on your day. But when you give your morning to God, when the first orientation of your heart is toward him, you set a trajectory for the day that the enemy will struggle to derail. Lamentations 3:20 to 2:3 says, "Through the Lord's mercies we are not consumed because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness." Every morning is a fresh outpouring of the mercy of God. Every morning is a new installment of his compassion. And those fresh mercies are not just for you to enjoy. They are fuel. They are the supply from which you draw to show mercy to others throughout the day. You come to God in the morning, you receive his mercy, and then you go into the day dispensing that same mercy to the people you encounter. You become a mercy distribution center. You become a daily delivery system for the goodness of God. Let me talk about something that I believe is essential for your character development and for your ability to reflect God's goodness. It is the discipline of the tongue. Proverbs 18:21 says, "Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit." Your words are not neutral. Every word you speak is either releasing life or releasing death. Every word is either building or demolishing. Every word is either reflecting the goodness of God or misrepresenting him. James 3 gives us one of the most vivid descriptions of the tongue. James says it is a small member, but it makes great boast. He says it is like a rudder that turns a great ship. He says it is like a spark that can set an entire forest on fire. And then he says with it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who have been made in the similitude of God. Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing, and his verdict in verse 10 is, "My brothers, this ought not to be so." This is not the design. The mouth that worships God on the morning of prayer should not be the same mouth that gossips, that slanders, that speaks with cruelty, that tears people down, that lies, that manipulates with words. Colossians 4:6 says, "Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one." Seasoned with grace, not bland, not harsh, not weaponized. Seasoned with grace. There should be something in the quality of your speech that is different from the world. When you speak to people, they should feel something, not just hear information. They should feel the weight of grace in your words. They should feel the kindness of God. They should feel seen. They should feel valued. They should feel like the person they are talking to has been with God. Acts 4:13 says that when they observed the boldness of Peter and John, they realized that they had been with Jesus. People should be able to look at you and conclude that you have been with God, not because you told them, not because you put it on your social media, but because there is something about the way you carry yourself, the way you speak, the way you treat people, the way you handle pressure that is not natural, that is supernatural. That can only be explained by the presence of God on the inside of you. I want to push even further this morning because I feel the spirit of God pressing on this. One of the greatest barriers to our actions reflecting God's goodness is the unresolved condition of our soul. Many believers are born again in spirit, but their soul, their mind, their will, their emotions has not been submitted to the sanctifying work of the Holy Spirit. And so what comes out in their actions is not the fruit of the spirit, but the fruit of an unsanctified soul, the fruit of childhood wounds that were never brought to the cross. The fruit of generational patterns that were never broken, the fruit of traumas that were buried under religious activity but never healed. Romans 8:13 says, "For if you live according to the flesh you will die, but if by the spirit you put to death the deeds of the body you will live." The putting to death of the deeds of the body is not a one-time event. It is a daily discipline. Every morning you come before God and you surrender the parts of you that are still operating according to the flesh. You say, "Lord, I see that in this area my responses are not reflecting you. I see that in this area my instincts are carnal. I see that in this area I am still being governed by fear and by pride and by insecurity. I bring it to you this morning. I yield it to the work of your spirit. Transform me, renew me, make me more like you." 2 Corinthians 3:18 says, "We all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the spirit of the Lord." Transformation is a process. It is a journey from glory to glory, but it is a real process. It is a genuine journey. And every day that you come before God with an unveiled face, every day that you open your heart to his word and his spirit without pretense and without performance, you are changed. Something shifts. Something gets refined. Something gets removed. Something gets added. And day by day, choice by choice, surrender by surrender, you look more and more like the God you serve. I want to close the preaching by coming back to where we started. The goodness of God. Because I want you to understand this morning that the goodness of God is not just a doctrine. It is not just a theological position. It is the very nature of the one who lives inside of you. First John 4 to 8 says God is love. Not God has love. Not God shows love sometimes. God is love. Love is not something God does. It is something God is. And if God lives inside of you, then love lives inside of you. Goodness lives inside of you. Patience lives inside of you. Kindness lives inside of you. The supply is not the problem. The yielding is the challenge. So this morning we are not asking God to give us something we do not have. We are asking him to remove every blockage that is preventing what is already in us from flowing out. We are asking him to break the dam. We are asking him to unclog the pipes. We are asking for a fresh release of the goodness that is already deposited in us by the Holy Spirit to flow freely into every situation we encounter today. Before we pray, I want you to do something. I want you to think about one specific person or situation that you will encounter today where the goodness of God through you is most needed. Maybe it is a difficult conversation you have been avoiding. Maybe it is someone you have been withholding forgiveness from. Maybe it is a colleague you have been dismissing. Maybe it is a family member you have been harsh with. Hold that person or that situation in your mind right now because the prayer we are about to pray is very targeted. It is going to land on that exact spot. Also, before we go into prayer, I want to encourage you to share this morning prayer with someone in your circle. Someone who needs this word today. Someone who is carrying the weight of misrepresenting God without knowing it. Someone who is heading into a difficult day and needs to be reminded that they are not going alone, that they are carrying the presence and the goodness of God with them. Send it to them. Let this be a blessing beyond this room. Now, let us pray. Let us enter into the presence of God with boldness this morning as Hebrews 4:16 instructs us. Let us come before him not with shame and not with fear, but with the confidence of sons and daughters who have been invited to come boldly to the throne of grace. Father, we come to you this morning. We come to you with the freshness of a new day in our hands. We come to you acknowledging that this morning your mercies are new. Your compassions have not failed. Your faithfulness is great and we are grateful. We are genuinely grateful to be alive on this side of the grave, on this side of eternity with the blood of Jesus still speaking in our favor. Father, the cry of our hearts this morning is simple and it is urgent. Let our actions today reflect your goodness. Not our mood, not our history, not our offense, not our flesh, but your goodness. Let the world that encounters us today encounter you through us. Let the kindness in our interactions be a direct reflection of the kindness that brought us to salvation. Let the patience in our responses be a direct reflection of the patience you extended to us in our worst moments. Let the integrity in our conduct be a declaration of the faithfulness of a God who has never broken a single promise he ever made to any man. Father, we come against every assignment of the enemy over our character this morning. We come against every spirit of offense, every spirit of pride, every spirit of self-centeredness, every spirit of impatience, every spirit of bitterness, every spirit of dishonesty in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, we command you to lose your hold on the people of God this morning. We declare that every chain that has kept us from being genuine reflections of God's goodness is broken right now by the power of the Holy Ghost. We plead the blood of Jesus over our mouths this morning. Lord, let every word that comes out of our mouths today be seasoned with grace. Let our words carry healing and not hurt. Let our words build and not destroy. Let our words encourage and not discourage. Let our words reflect the wisdom that comes from above that James 3:17 describes as pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy. Lord, that is the wisdom we want to speak with today. That is the grace we want to dispense with every word. Father, we pray now for the specific situations and the specific people that are in our minds this morning. Lord, you know who they are. You know the history. You know the wounds. You know the complexity. And we bring it all to you right now. We surrender every right to retaliate. We surrender every right to withhold. We surrender every excuse for not reflecting your goodness in that specific situation. And we ask you, Lord, give us the supernatural grace to show up in that moment and be a demonstration of who you are. Give us the words. Give us the tone. Give us the posture. Give us the humility. Give us the love that is strong enough to cover the offense that was committed. Lord, we pray for a fresh baptism of love this morning. Pour your love into our hearts by the Holy Ghost according to Romans 5:2-5. Let it overflow, Lord. Let it be so abundant that it spills over into every relationship we carry, every interaction we have, every environment we enter. Let us leave love residue wherever we go. Let people feel the warmth of God's presence simply by spending time with us. Let them leave our company better than they came. Let them leave encouraged, valued, seen, and pointed toward you. Father, for the believer who is in a difficult workplace environment today, we pray for supernatural grace. We pray for the grace to maintain your standard in a system that is pressuring them to lower it. Give them the courage of Daniel. Give them the excellence of Joseph. Give them the wisdom to navigate every trap that the enemy has set. And Lord, even as you were with Daniel in Babylon, be with them in their Babylon today. Let your presence be so tangible in their lives that even their Nebuchadnezzar cannot deny that the God they serve is with them. We pray for fathers and mothers this morning who are raising children in a home. Lord, let the goodness of God be visible in the way they parent today. Let patience be the atmosphere in their homes. Let love be the language spoken. Let integrity be the curriculum being taught not in words, but in the living demonstration of parents who walk what they talk. Let the children in those homes grow up with a clear picture of who God is because they saw him modeled in the behavior of their parents every single day. For the young person heading into a peer environment today where compromise is cool and righteousness is mocked, Father, strengthen them. Let them find more value in your approval than in the approval of their peers. Give them the courage to be different. Let their difference attract rather than alienate. Let their consistency build a testimony that eventually opens doors for them to share the reason for the hope that is in them as 1 Peter 3:15 instructs. Father, seal this morning. Let the word that was ministered not fall on hard ground. Let it fall on good soil and bring forth fruit 30, 60, and a hundredfold as Jesus described in the parable of the sower. Let transformation begin this morning. Let it be progressive. Let it be real. Let it not be an emotional experience that fades by noon. Let it be a genuine work of the spirit that endures, that strengthens, that grows day by day until the day when we see you face to face and we hear those words, "Well done, good and faithful servant." We receive by faith today the grace to reflect your goodness, Father. We receive it. We do not merely hope for it. We do not simply wish for it. We receive it as a present reality. The fruit of the spirit is operating in our lives right now. Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. These are not ambitions. These are realities in the lives of men and women who are yielded to the Holy Spirit and we choose to yield today. Now, make this declaration out of your mouth this morning. Say it like you mean it. Say it from the deepest part of your being. Father, today is not a wasted day. Today is not an ordinary day. Today is a day you have specifically arranged for me to be a carrier of your goodness into the earth. I step into this day with intentionality. I step into it with the consciousness of your presence. I step into it knowing that everywhere I go, I carry an atmosphere of heaven. I carry your love. I carry your peace. I carry your wisdom. I carry your excellence. I carry your integrity. I declare that my actions today will tell the right story about you, God. My responses will be governed by your spirit and not by my flesh. My words will be measured by grace and not by my emotions. My decisions will be guided by your word and not by the pressures of culture. I am a living epistle. Known and read of all men. And today the world will read something about you in my life that draws them closer to you and not farther away. I declare that every barrier between my inner man and my outer conduct is dismantled by the power of the Holy Ghost. There is no more contradiction between what I believe and how I behave. There is no more gap between my Sunday testimony and my Monday conduct. My life is integrated. My character is consistent. My conduct is consecrated. And the name of Jesus Christ is being glorified through my life today. Father, receive the glory from this day. Take every interaction, every conversation, every decision, every act of kindness, every moment of patience, every choice of integrity, and receive it as worship because that is what it is. When I represent you correctly in the earth, I am worshiping you. When I love the unlovable because you first loved me, I am worshiping you. When I forgive the undeserving because I myself received undeserved forgiveness, I am worshiping you. Let my life be a living act of worship today in the name of Jesus. In the great and mighty name of Jesus Christ, the son of the living God, we pray. Amen. Amen. Amen. Go and make this day count. Go and carry him well. Go and let the world see that your God is good.
